function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t something that was “discovered” by a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since ancient times. However, several key figures helped uncover its nature and harness it:

| Person | Contribution |
|--------|--------------|
| **Thales of Miletus** (c. 600 BCE) | First recorded observations of static electricity (rubber rubbed with fur). |
| **William Gilbert** (late 1500s) | Coined the word *electricus* (from Greek *elektron*, amber) and distinguished between magnetism and static electricity. |
| **Benjamin Franklin** (mid‑1700s) | Conducted the famous kite experiment, proving that lightning is electrical and introduced the concepts of positive/negative charge. |
| **Alessandro Volta** (1800) | Invented the first chemical battery (the voltaic pile), providing a steady source of electric current. |
| **Michael Faraday** (1830s‑1840s) | Discovered electromagnetic induction, laying the groundwork for electric generators and motors. |
| **James Clerk Maxwell** (1860s) | Unified electricity and magnetism into a single theory of electromagnetism. |

So while no single individual “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of these scientists—and many others—led to our modern understanding and use of electric power.
